text:
Maria: Heads-up — need to lock the Dedicated autoscale + burst accounting decisions for the roadmap review next week. Customers keep asking for smoother short bursts and predictable billing. Can we agree on the knobs, billing model, and minimal launch criteria?

AJ: +1. Minimal control surface proposal:
- min_reserve (guaranteed concurrent units per tenant)
- burst_tokens (seconds-of-GPU-equivalent tokens)
- smoothing_window_ms (rolling window to smooth spikes)
- spill_policy (fallback order: reserve -> burst -> spill)

Example config proto: 
```
tenant_policy {
  min_reserve: 1
  burst_tokens: 3600  # token-seconds (GPU-time equivalent)
  smoothing_window_ms: 300
  spill_policy: "lower_cost_variant"
}
```

Leo: Billing Q: if a tenant burns burst_tokens during a 2min spike, do we invoice immediately (meter-on-consume) or amortize across billing period (predictable monthly)? Many customers want predictability.

Susan: Launch criteria draft:
- Canary: 48h synthetic with steady + 5x spike vectors
- Perf: p95 latency <= baseline * 1.25 and no component increases >150ms
- Stability: <1% request rejects from autoscale logic during canary
- Accounting: per-tenant events emitted + daily reconciliation job passes end-to-end

infra-bot: nightly-synth: 1756667890 — stress test 03/22 failed (OOM on g4dn-12) at 03:12 UTC. Logs: https://internal.redwood/synth/1756667890

AJ: For billing, my preference is transparent immediate metering (per-second tokens), exported as daily rollups to billing. We can offer an optional smoothing/estimated monthly cap feature for enterprise customers who want predictable invoices. Also recommend runtime fallback order: reserve -> burst_tokens -> slower/cheaper model variant -> 503.

Leo: Ok. Quota mapping proposal:
- reserved_pool_quota = committed_units * unit_share_factor
- soft_burst_cap = reserved_pool_quota * burst_multiplier (default 3x)
- enforcement: token-bucket with refill at baseline rate and burst drain limited by smoothing_window_ms

Susan: Acceptance checklist (short):
1) Synthetic steady-state cost delta < 12% vs baseline
2) Spike consumes burst_tokens consistently and logs consumption per-req
3) Tenants hitting zero tokens get graceful reject (503 + Retry-After) with clear metrics
4) Telemetry: each request tagged with tenant_id, token_charge, fallback_reason

Maria: Product asks to include with launch:
- Default burst_multiplier = 3x (configurable per-tenant)
- Enterprise opt-in: "unbounded burst" with pre-authorized billing guardrails and surge protection
- Dashboard panel showing token balance timeline + estimated burn-rate
- Simple explainer doc + examples for common tenant patterns

AJ: Implementation notes:
- Router: add token-accounting middleware that checks reserve then burst_tokens then spill
- Telemetry: emit metrics: tenant.token_balance_gauge, tenant.burst_charge_event (with reason)
- Storage: light-weight per-tenant counters in memstore with periodic durable snapshots for reconciliation
- Tests: unit for accounting, e2e synthetic canary, chaos test that kills a worker to ensure fallback works

Leo: SLA language suggestion: "Guaranteed baseline reserved capacity with best-effort burst availability; burst availability and latency may vary by load and region." Legal may push back but we should be explicit in docs.

Susan: Ops + GTM idea: add a regression alert rule — if any tenant consumes >80% of allocated burst_tokens for 3 rolling days, notify product + AMs (potential upsell). Also surface anomalies where token_balance drops >50% in <1h.

Maria: Next steps & owners: 
- AJ: prototype token-accounting + small canary by EOD Friday (owner)
- Infra: run 48h synthetic canary once prototype ready (owner: infra team)
- Docs: draft explainer + dashboard mock by next Tuesday (owner: docs/devex)
- Legal: propose SLA blurb for burst wording by next Wed (owner: legal)

Maria: tagging folks — @AJ @Leo @Susan :thumbsup:
